CAS — 4969-02-2 (metixene); 1553-34-0 (anhydrous metixene hydrochloride); 7081-40-5 (metixene hydrochlo- ride monohydrate). ATC — N04AA03. ATC Vet — QN04AA03. (metixene) Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Metixene Hydrochloride). A white or almost white, crystalline or fine crystalline powder. Soluble in water, in alcohol, and in dichloromethane. A 1.8% solution in water has a pH of 4.4 to 5.8. Protect from light. Profile Metixene hydrochloride is a tertiary antimuscarinic with actions similar to those of atropine (p.1219); it also has antihistaminic and direct antispasmodic properties. It is used for the symptomatic treatment of parkinsonism (p.791), including the alleviation of the extrapyramidal syndrome in- duced by drugs such as phenothiazines, but, like other antimus- carinics, is of no value against tardive dyskinesias. The usual oral dose of metixene hydrochloride is 2.5 mg three times daily ini- tially, gradually increased according to response to a total of 15 to 60 mg daily in divided doses. Metixene hydrochloride has also been used in preparations to re- lieve gastrointestinal spasms.
